title:
This type describes a single type declaration language (DSL) keyword, which is useful for code formatting. Note that
keywords in the DSL are _not_ reserved words. For example a method can be named "type" (and in fact
{@link WithType#type there is one}).

Also note that some keywords are actually two words, for example "with millis" and "not remixable". In these cases,
neither of the individual words are keywords, only both together.

Finally, there is keyword-like syntax for method claims. For example "js-browser" at the end of a declaration may be
styled as a keyword, but again "js" by itself is not a reserved word and "js-browser" in other context is an
expression that subtracts the "browser" field from the "js" field.

To perform more targeted syntax highlighting, these should be applied only when the following token is not a ':'
(negative lookahead). For claim keywords, they may be followed by a dash and any word characters or additional
dashes, plus an optional version, and can appear only at the end of a line.

@see type-dsl.c3doc.md
@see ui-dsl.c3doc.md
